lessons.M1.L1: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison.
lessons.M1.L2: Recognize a digit represents 10 times the value of what it represents in the place to its right.
lessons.M1.L3: Name numbers within 1 billion by building understanding of the place value chart and placement of commas for naming base thousand units.
lessons.M1.L4: Read and write multi-digit numbers using base ten numerals, number names, and expanded notation.
lessons.M1.L5: Compare numbers based on meanings of the digits using >, <, or = to record the comparison.
lessons.M1.L6: Find 1, 10, and 100 thousand and 1, 10, and 100 million more and less than a given number.
lessons.M1.L7: Round multi-digit numbers to the thousands place using the vertical number line.
lessons.M1.L8: Round multi-digit numbers to any place using the vertical number line
lessons.M1.L9: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit numbers to any place value.
lessons.M1.L10: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit numbers to any place value using real world applications.
lessons.M1.L11: Use place value understanding to fluently add multi-digit whole numbers using the standard addition algorithm, and apply the algorithm to solve word problems using strip diagrams.
lessons.M1.L12: Solve multi-step word problems using the standard addition algorithm modeled with strip diagrams, and assess the reasonableness of answers using rounding.
lessons.M1.L13: Use place value understanding to decompose to smaller units once using the standard subtraction algorithm, and apply the algorithm to solve word problems using strip diagrams.
lessons.M1.L14: Use place value understanding to decompose to smaller units up to three times using the standard subtraction algorithm, and apply the algorithm to solve word problems using strip diagrams.
lessons.M1.L16: Solve two-step word problems using the standard subtraction algorithm fluently modeled with strip diagrams, and assess the reasonableness of answers using rounding
lessons.M1.L18: Solve multi-step word problems modeled with strip diagrams, and assess the reasonableness of answers using rounding.
lessons.M2.L1: Express metric length measurements in terms of a smaller unit; model and solve addition and subtraction word problems involving metric length
lessons.M2.L2: Express metric mass measurements in terms of a smaller unit; model and solve addition and subtraction word problems involving metric mass.
lessons.M2.L3: Express metric capacity measurements in terms of a smaller unit; model and solve addition and subtraction word problems involving metric capacity
lessons.M2.L4: Know and relate metric units to place value units in order to express measurements in different units.
lessons.M2.L5: Use addition and subtraction to solve multi-step word problems involving length, mass, and capacity.
lessons.M3.L1: Investigate and use the formulas for area and perimeter of rectangles.
lessons.M3.L2: Solve multiplicative comparison word problems by applying the area and perimeter formulas.
lessons.M3.L3: Demonstrate understanding of area and perimeter formulas by solving multi-step real-world problems.
lessons.M3.L4: Interpret and represent patterns when multiplying by 10, 100, and 1,000 in arrays and numerically.
lessons.M3.L5: Multiply multiples of 10, 100, and 1,000 by single digits, recognizing patterns.
lessons.M3.L6: Multiply two-digit multiples of 10 by two-digit multiples of 10 with the area model.
lessons.M3.L7: Use place value disks to represent two-digit by one-digit multiplication.
lessons.M3.L8: Extend the use of place value disks to represent three- and four-digit by one-digit multiplication.
lessons.M3.L9: Multiply three- and four-digit numbers by one-digit numbers applying the standard algorithm.
lessons.M3.L11: Connect the area model and the partial products method to the standard algorithm.
lessons.M3.L12: Solve two-step word problems, including multiplicative comparison
lessons.M3.L13: Use multiplication, addition, or subtraction to solve multi-step word problems.
lessons.M3.L14: Solve division word problems with remainders
lessons.M3.L15: Understand and solve division problems with a remainder using the array and area models.
lessons.M3.L16: Understand and solve two-digit dividend division problems with a remainder in the ones place by using place value disks.
lessons.M3.L17: Represent and solve division problems requiring decomposing a remainder in the tens.
lessons.M3.L18: Find whole number quotients and remainders.
lessons.M3.L20: Solve division problems without remainders using the area model.
lessons.M3.L22: Divide multiples of 10, 100, and 1,000 by single-digit numbers.
lessons.M3.L23: Represent and solve division problems with up to a three-digit dividend numerically and with place value disks requiring decomposing a remainder in the hundreds place.
lessons.M3.L24: Represent and solve three-digit dividend division with divisors of 2, 3, 4, and 5 numerically.
lessons.M3.L25: Represent numerically four-digit dividend division with divisors of 2, 3, 4, and 5, decomposing a remainder up to three times.
lessons.M3.L26: Solve division problems with a zero in the dividend or with a zero in the quotient.
lessons.M3.L27: Interpret division word problems as either number of groups unknown or group size unknown.
lessons.M3.L28: Interpret and find whole number quotients and remainders to solve one-step division word problems with larger divisors of 6, 7, 8, and 9.
lessons.M3.L29: Explain the connection of the area model of division to the long division algorithm for three- and four-digit dividends.
lessons.M3.L30: Multiply two-digit multiples of 10 by two-digit numbers using a place value chart.
lessons.M3.L31: Multiply two-digit multiples of 10 by two-digit numbers using the area model.
lessons.M3.L32: Multiply two-digit by two-digit numbers using four partial products.
lessons.M3.L33: Transition from four partial products to the standard algorithm for two-digit by two-digit multiplication.
lessons.M3.L34: Transition from four partial products to the standard algorithm for two-digit by two-digit multiplication.
lessons.M4.L1: Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, and angles. Recognize them in various contexts and familiar figures.
lessons.M4.L2: Use right angles to determine whether angles are equal to, greater than, or less than right angles. Draw right, obtuse, and acute angles.
lessons.M4.L3: Identify, define, and draw perpendicular lines.
lessons.M4.L4: Identify, define, and draw parallel lines.
lessons.M4.L5: Use a circular protractor to understand a 1-degree angle as 1/360 of any circle. Explore benchmark angles using the protractor.
lessons.M4.L6: Use varied protractors to distinguish angle measure from length measurement.
lessons.M4.L7: Measure and draw angles. Sketch given angle measures, and verify with a protractor.
lessons.M4.L10: Use the addition of adjacent angle measures to solve problems using a letter for the unknown angle measure.
lessons.M4.L12: Recognize lines of symmetry for given two-dimensional figures. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.
lessons.M4.L13: Analyze and classify triangles based on angle measure.
lessons.M4.L14: Define and construct triangles from given criteria.
lessons.M4.L15: Classify quadrilaterals based on parallel and perpendicular lines and the presence or absence of angles of a specified size.
lessons.M4.L16: Reason about attributes to construct quadrilaterals on square or triangular grid paper.
lessons.M5.L1: Decompose fractions as a sum of unit fractions using strip diagrams.
lessons.M5.L2: Decompose fractions as a sum of unit fractions using strip diagrams.
lessons.M5.L4: Decompose unit fractions using area models to show equivalence.
lessons.M5.L5: Decompose fractions using area models to show equivalence.
lessons.M5.L6: Use the area model and multiplication to show the equivalence of two fractions.
lessons.M5.L8: Use the area model and division to show the equivalence of two fractions.
lessons.M5.L10: Explain fraction equivalence using a strip diagram and the number line, and relate that to the use of multiplication and division.
lessons.M5.L11: Reason using benchmarks to compare two fractions on the number line.
lessons.M5.L13: Find common units or number of units to compare two Fractions.
lessons.M5.L16: Use visual models to add and subtract two fractions with the same units, including subtracting from one whole.
lessons.M5.L17: Add and subtract more than two fractions.
lessons.M5.L19: Add a fraction less than 1 to, or subtract a fraction less than 1 from, a whole number using decomposition and visual models.
lessons.M5.L20: Decompose and compose fractions greater than 1 to express them in various forms.
lessons.M5.L22: Compare fractions greater than 1 by reasoning using benchmark fractions.
lessons.M5.L23: Compare fractions greater than 1 by creating common numerators or denominators.
lessons.M5.L24: Solve word problems with dot plots.
lessons.M5.L25: Estimate sums and differences using benchmark numbers.
lessons.M5.L26: Add a mixed number and a fraction.
lessons.M5.L28: Subtract a fraction from a mixed number.
lessons.M5.L29: Subtract a mixed number from a mixed number
lessons.M6.L1: Use metric measurement to model the decomposition of one whole into tenths.
lessons.M6.L2: Use metric measurement and area models to represent tenths as fractions greater than 1 and decimal numbers.
lessons.M6.L3: Represent mixed numbers with units of tens, ones, and tenths with place value disks, on the number line, and in expanded notation.
lessons.M6.L4: Use meters to model the decomposition of one whole into hundredths. Represent and count hundredths.
lessons.M6.L5: Model the equivalence of tenths and hundredths using the area model and place value disks.
lessons.M6.L6: Use the area model and number line to represent mixed numbers with units of ones, tenths, and hundredths in fraction and decimal forms.
lessons.M6.L7: Model mixed numbers with units of hundreds, tens, ones, tenths, and hundredths in expanded notation and on the place value chart.
lessons.M6.L9: Use the place value chart and metric measurement to compare decimals and answer comparison questions.
lessons.M6.L10: Use area models and the number line to compare decimal numbers, and record comparisons using < , > , and = .
lessons.M6.L12: Apply place value understanding to add tenths and hundredths.
lessons.M6.L13: Apply place value understanding to subtract tenths and Hundredths.
lessons.M6.L14: Solve word problems involving the addition and subtraction of measurements in decimal form.
lessons.M6.L15: Express money amounts given in various forms as decimal Numbers.
lessons.M6.L17: Understand the difference between fixed and variable expenses for the purpose of allocating a weekly allowance.
lessons.M6.L18: Solve word problems, including the calculation of profit.

lessons.M7.L2: Create conversion tables for length, weight, and capacity units using measurement tools, and use the tables to solve problems.
lessons.M7.L3: Create conversion tables for units of time, and use the tables to solve problems.
lessons.M7.L4: Solve multiplicative comparison word problems using measurement conversion tables.

lessons.M7.L8: Solve problems involving mixed units of weight.
